paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. Jesus looked at a man who couldn't walk and started with something deeper than his legs. He said, "Take courage, son; your sins are forgiven." (Matthew 9:2) The biggest need that man had was one nobody could see, and Jesus went straight to it.

Then the scribes had a whole meeting in their heads, and Jesus knew what they were thinking. (Matthew 9:3-4) He asked which is easier, to say sins are forgiven or to say, "Get up and walk" (Matthew 9:5). Then He did it "so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" (Matthew 9:6). Anyone can SAY words nobody can check, but Jesus backed His up where everybody could see, and the man walked home.

So what does that mean for you? It means the One who can heal a body is the One who has authority to forgive your sins, and you can trust Him with both. The men who carried their friend showed faith by bringing him to Jesus, and Jesus saw it. (Matthew 9:2) Bring Him the stuff you can't fix on your own, baker, and when you see what He does, do what the crowds did and glorify God. (Matthew 9:8)
